narrative.overview:
The interface feels like a calm service-counter worksheet: warm paper, dark graphite rules, compact typography, and dense but legible records. It supports both storefront discovery and operator audit work without changing visual identity, keeping every claim, control, and state visibly grounded in commerce data.

The system is flat and evidence-led. Structure comes from ruled edges, tonal paper layers, tabular figures, and precise alignment; amber marks intent or selection, while green and red remain semantic. Arabic and English are equal compositions, with direction changing the flow rather than the information hierarchy.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper rather than clinical white.
Hairline graphite rules rather than floating containers.
Compact Alexandria typography across Arabic and Latin scripts.
Amber selection, green success and availability, red failure and recovery.
Dense, auditable data that becomes stacked cards on narrow screens.
Synthetic assets and evaluation limits are labeled, never implied away.

rules.name: The Semantic Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber communicates intent or selection; green communicates availability or success; red communicates failure, invalidity, or destructive recovery. Never use those colors as interchangeable decoration.

rules.name: The Warm Canvas Rule
rules.body: Keep the page and controls within the paper family; pure white is reserved for tiny contrast details, not major surfaces.

rules.name: The Alexandria Rule
rules.body: Use Alexandria at weights 400, 500, or 600 for both Arabic and English; reserve heavier emphasis for numeric prices already established in product cards.

rules.name: The Evidence Numeral Rule
rules.body: Prices, counts, dates, quantities, and policy values use tabular numerals; Latin identifiers and supplier references are isolated LTR inside RTL copy.

rules.name: The Logical Direction Rule
rules.body: Mirror flow with document direction and logical properties; do not manually reverse content order or duplicate separate Arabic and English layouts.

rules.name: The Reference Exception Rule
rules.body: `.impeccable/mocks/comp-a.png` is an LTR reference. The storefront comparison score of 58.53% is an approved RTL composition exception, not a numerical pass; preserve equivalent hierarchy and task order rather than chasing pixel symmetry.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Static hierarchy is made with rules and tonal paper layers; shadow appears only for hover, fixed-overlay separation, or an active recording signal.

rules.name: The Ruled Rectangle Rule
rules.body: Use a one-pixel graphite or soft-rule border and square corners for all primary containers and controls; do not soften the workbench into rounded cards.

dos: Do preserve the warm paper, graphite rule, and compact Alexandria foundation across storefront and back-office screens.
Do use logical CSS properties, document direction, bidi isolation, and explicit LTR spans for Latin identifiers so Arabic and English remain equal experiences.
Do keep statuses text-labeled and pair amber, green, or red with borders and surface tones rather than color alone.
Do transform dense inventory rows into labeled mobile audit cards at 700px instead of forcing a 960px table through a phone viewport.
Do label synthetic product imagery and synthetic operational evidence at the point where users encounter it.
donts: Don't introduce rounded dashboard cards, glass effects, decorative gradients, or persistent ambient shadows.
Don't treat the 58.53% comparison against `.impeccable/mocks/comp-a.png` as a pass; it is an approved RTL composition exception to an LTR reference.
Don't use amber, green, or red as arbitrary decoration or as the only carrier of state meaning.
Don't fabricate logos, real-product photography, reviews, discounts, production prices, or operational-quality claims.
Don't remove visible focus, text alternatives, retry paths, reduced-motion behavior, or equivalent text paths for image and voice search.
